title: Chapter 4 – ABC, Lean, and Costs of Quality (Objectives)
notes: Develop and use departmental overhead rates to allocate indirect costs
Understand the limitations of a simple departmental overhead rate allocation
Develop and use activity-based costing (ABC) to allocate indirect costs
Understand the benefits and limitations of ABC/ABM systems

flashcards.back: Separate POHRs for each department to better reflect resource use and complexity.
Dept POHR = Est. dept MOH ÷ Est. dept allocation base.

flashcards.front: Limitations of single plantwide or simple departmental rates?
flashcards.back: May cause cost distortion if drivers don’t reflect how products consume resources.

flashcards.front: When do simple rates work poorly?
flashcards.back: Product diversity, high overhead, complex processes, automation.
Trace costs to activities, then to products using activity cost drivers (volume and non-volume).
Identify activities → assign costs to activity pools → choose cost drivers → compute rates → assign to products.
Unit-, Batch-, Product-, and Facility-level activities.
Improves process efficiency, pricing, product mix, and highlights non-value-added activities.
Costly to implement/maintain; requires good data; benefits vary with context.
